method: captured and timed variants of the REAL block using the model's own run_vx / run_ax / a2v_cross_attn / v2a_cross_attn switches, so no numerical source was touched; outputs are meaningless, only timing is

clip_cost.note: 48 blocks, 8 stage-1 steps plus 3 stage-2 steps

findings: The audio stream is 29% of every block while carrying only 26 tokens, and its cost barely changes when the video stream goes from 64 to 256 tokens (0.807 -> 0.897 ms), so it is weight and kernel-overhead bound, not token bound.

At 131 MB of weights the audio stream should take 0.244 ms; it takes 0.807, which is 3.3x above roofline -- the worst ratio anywhere in the model. The video stream is 2.2x and the two cross attentions 2.3x.

Nothing in the block is near roofline. The whole block is 1.92x above, and that is consistent with small kernels paying fixed GPU-side cost that graph replay does not remove: a kernel reading 8 MB needs 15 us at roofline, so a ~25 us floor per kernel alone explains the ratio.

lever_implied.idea: The video and audio streams are independent within a block until a2v/v2a, so the audio path could run on an idle card concurrently with the video path. This changes no arithmetic -- same weights, same order, same reductions -- so it is lossless in principle, and the two cards were measured to replay graphs with perfect concurrency (factor 1.999).
lever_implied.arithmetic: block becomes max(video 1.978, audio 0.807) + cross 0.41 + transfers, against 2.761 today: about 0.37 ms per block before communication. Two activation exchanges per block cost roughly 0.1 ms, so the net is about 0.27 ms per block, or 0.14 s per clip.
lever_implied.verdict: Real and lossless in principle, but ~0.14 s for a substantial restructuring of the block into two device-resident halves. Recorded, not built.

limitations: two probe blocks (0 and 24) of 48, though they agree to within 2%
the switch variants change what the block computes; only timing is meaningful
the weight-byte figures per stream are derived from the checkpoint shapes, not measured
